chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahboub from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat from Abu Sarah from Hind al-Sarraj who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'May Allah improve you. I used to carry weapons to the people of Syria and sell them to them. When Allah made this matter known to me, I felt constrained by that and said: I will not carry to the enemies of Allah.' He said: 'Carry to them, for Allah repels by them our enemy and your enemy, meaning the Romans; and sell to them. So when war is between us, do not carry. For whoever carries to our enemy weapons with which they assist themselves against us, then he is a polytheist.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling weapons to non-Shia Muslims or Romans according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) distinguishes between strategic trade with external enemies like the Romans, who are not immediate adversaries, and selling arms to those who will use them against the Shia, which constitutes a major sin. This ruling highlights the pragmatic approach of the Imams regarding economic engagement with non-Shia powers during peacetime, while emphasizing the spiritual gravity of aiding in the community's defeat during conflict.
